BorrowedThreads.description: The table form of a mount's threads.

max.description: The most requests the mount runs at once, on its reserved threads and borrowed ones together.

Build.description: The `[tool.muru.build]` table: when and how the release's environment is built from the lock. `when` is read by `muructl run` and the daemon alike; the rest describes the deployment flavour, which development ignores.

groups.description: Dependency groups beyond the defaults; dev is never included.

source_builds.description: Allow sdists to be built on the node.

when.description: When an environment is built: `auto` builds a missing one and leaves an existing one alone, `always` builds on every start and on a lock change, `never` builds nothing. `muructl serve` never builds one.

oneOf.description: Build a missing environment; leave an existing one alone at start, and under `muructl run` build when the lock changes.
Build before every start too.
Build nothing.

Bytecode.description: Where compiled bytecode goes for a daemon-managed release.

oneOf.description: A writable directory of the release's own under the state directory, so nothing lands in the source tree (the default).
`__pycache__` beside the source, as Python does by default; what a release with precompiled bytecode uses.
No bytecode is written.

except.description: Files that get no-cache instead, by pattern on their path within the route.

max_age.description: How long clients may keep a file, for example 1y or 1h.

default.description: The value when none is given.

description.description: What the value is, for `muructl command list` and prompts.

pattern.description: A regular expression the whole value must match.

required.description: The command refuses to run without it.

secret.description: The value is never shown, logged or put in an event, and may only be used in `env`.

CommandTable.description: A command an application declares, the `[tool.muru.commands.NAME]` or `[app.NAME.release.ID.commands.NAME]` table: a program to run, or a Python callable to call, with the release.

call.description: A callable as module:function, called with the inputs as keyword arguments, instead of `run`.

description.description: What the command does, for `muructl command list`.

env.description: Environment variables for this command alone, over the release's, with `{name}` where an input's value goes.

exclusive.description: Run one at a time for the application: a run asked for while one is under way is refused.

inputs.description: The values the command takes, by name.

run.description: The program and its arguments, run without a shell, with `{name}` where an input's value goes; `python` is the release's interpreter.

timeout.description: How long it may run before it is stopped, for example 10m; no limit when absent.

Count.description: A count given as a number or as a word such as `auto`.

EnvValue.description: A value in an `[env]` table: the text itself, or a reference to a secret in a store, delivered as the variable or, with `as = 'file'`, as a file whose path is in `NAME_FILE`.

ErrorOverride.description: Replacing an application's own error responses with error pages, the `error_override` table.

statuses.description: The statuses whose responses are replaced.

when.description: When a listed response is replaced: `all` (the default), `empty_body`, `not_json` or `html_only`.

ErrorPage.description: A custom error page: one entry of an `error_pages` table, keyed by status (`404`) or status and reason (`"503:maintenance"`). Exactly one of `file`, `template` and `path` is given.

content_type.description: The content type of a template.

file.description: A file sent as the body, with the content type its name implies. A release's page may be a path relative to its source directory; elsewhere the path is absolute.

path.description: An application path the edge asks for the page, as an internal sub-request that sees `REDIRECT_STATUS` and `muru.error_reason`.

template.description: A template the edge renders, with `{status}`, `{title}`, `{reason}`, `{description}`, `{request_id}`, `{retry_after}`, `{host}` and `{path}` filled in.

FactoryPhase.description: When a factory entrypoint is called.

oneOf.description: In each worker, after the post_fork hook.
Once in the host, during preload.

Group.description: A worker group, the `[app.NAME.release.ID.groups.NAME]` or `[tool.muru.groups.NAME]` table: the paths it serves and its own sizes. Paths not claimed by a group go to the default group, which is the release's own settings.

concurrency.description: Requests an ASGI worker's event loop takes at once.

match.description: What the group asks of a request beside its path: the client classes, hosts and methods it takes, each list any of its entries; a group asking more comes before one asking less, and a group with lists and no `paths` takes every path.

max_lifetime.description: How long a worker of the group lives before it is replaced, for example 1h, with jitter.

max_requests.description: Requests a worker of the group serves before it is replaced, with jitter.

memory.description: The group's own memory policy, each key the release's when absent.

mounts.description: The named mounts the group's workers serve, beside the default mount, which every worker serves; every mount when absent. The group's paths must lie within them.

optional.description: Whether the release is ready without the group's workers: its requests wait until one listens.

paths.description: Path prefixes, with an optional trailing `*`; the most specific match across all groups wins.

scaling.description: How the group is scaled; static when absent.

sync_threads.description: Threads for synchronous code called from an ASGI application.

timeouts.description: The group's own timeouts, each the release's when absent; `shutdown_timeout` and `websocket_drain_grace` belong to the release.

GroupMatch.description: The requests a worker group takes for its paths: every list given must name the request's class, host or method.

host.description: Hosts: a virtual host's name or a name it answers to, or under `muructl run` the name the request carries.

Handoff.description: The interface a release's or a mount's requests may be handed to: ASGI from a WSGI application, WSGI from an ASGI one.

oneOf.description: Continue the request as an ASGI application on the event loop.
Continue the request as a WSGI callable on the thread pool.
Detect from the callable: a coroutine function or an object with an `async def __call__` is ASGI, anything else WSGI.
ASGI 3.
gRPC services: the entrypoint is a registration function given a server to add grpcio servicers to.
Everything.
Informational messages and above.
Python's default: warnings and above.
Errors and above.
Only critical messages.

Logging.description: The `[logging]` table: how Python logging is set up in the workers.

Maintenance.description: What maintenance mode lets through, the `maintenance` table of a release.

bypass_cookie.description: A `name=value` cookie that lets a client through.

exempt_addresses.description: Client addresses, or ranges in CIDR form, served as usual.

exempt_paths.description: Path prefixes served as usual while the application is in maintenance.

retry_after.description: The `Retry-After` the maintenance page carries, for example 5m.

Measure.description: How a worker's memory is measured.

oneOf.description: Unique set size: pages no other process shares, the default, since preloaded pages are shared copy-on-write.
Proportional set size: shared pages counted in proportion.
Resident set size: every resident page.

Memory.description: The `[memory]` table of a release or a `[tool.muru]` table: the limits a worker's memory is held to.

hard_limit.description: Over this the worker leaves routing at once and is replaced, for example 1200MB.
hard_limit.x-default: off; under `muructl serve` with a memory limit, a share of it

measure.description: What is measured: uss (the default), pss or rss.

reclaim_first.description: Whether to collect garbage and trim the heap before recycling over the soft limit.

soft_for.description: How long the worker may stay over the soft limit.

soft_limit.description: Over this for soft_for, the worker reclaims and then recycles, for example 800MB; off when absent.

Mount.description: A mount, the `[app.NAME.release.ID.mounts.NAME]` or `[tool.muru.mounts.NAME]` table: a path served by another entrypoint in the same workers. The release's own entrypoint is the default mount at /.

accel_redirect.description: Treat an `X-Accel-Redirect` response header from the mount as an internal redirect.

accept_redirects_from.description: Other applications whose internal redirects may reach the mount when it is internal; the release's own always may.

cgi_local_redirect.description: Treat a 200 response with a `Location` starting with `/` and no body as an internal redirect, the CGI convention.

concurrency.description: Requests an ASGI mount runs at once on each worker, slots of its own at the edge; it shares the event loop's concurrency when absent.

handoff.description: The interface the mount's requests may be handed to; none when absent.

interface.description: The interface, when declared rather than detected.

internal.description: Reachable only through internal redirects: a client's request for its path is answered 404.

max_connections.description: Open WebSockets an ASGI mount holds at once on each worker, apart from the requests it runs; each holds a request slot when absent.

path.description: The path prefix; the longest wins, on segment boundaries. A gRPC mount has none: its calls are matched by service name.

sendfile_header.description: A second response header honoured as `X-Muru-Sendfile` is, such as `X-Sendfile`.

sendfile_roots.description: Directories a path in an `X-Muru-Sendfile` response header must lie in for the edge to serve the file; the release's when absent, and an empty list refuses every hint.

threads.description: Threads of the mount's own, for a WSGI or gRPC mount; it shares the worker's pool when absent.

anyOf.description: A pool of this many threads, used by the mount alone.
Reserved threads, and shared ones borrowed up to a maximum.

MountThreads.description: A mount's own threads: a fixed pool, `threads = 4`, or a reserved minimum that borrows threads of the shared pool up to a maximum, `threads = { reserved = 2, max = 6 }`.

Preload.description: Whether the application is imported in the host before forking.

oneOf.description: Preload when the import check passes, otherwise import per worker.
Preload, and fail the release when the import check does not pass.
Import in every worker.

PythonLogging.description: The `[logging.python]` table: what loggers without handlers of their own do, set before the application is imported.

capture_warnings.description: Whether warnings.warn goes through the py.warnings logger.

format.description: The format of the platform handler: standard, json, or a logging format string.

RunPort.description: A port of the run table: a number, or `auto` for a free one, as the `--port` and `--https-port` flags take it.

RunSettings.description: The `[tool.muru.run]` table of a pyproject.toml, or `[run]` in a muru.toml and in muru.local.toml: how `muructl run` serves this project, with a key for each flag of the command that describes the serving rather than the application. The daemon ignores it. Lists add across the layers, as a list flag adds to a key.

access_log.description: Which requests the access log writes: `on` (the default), `errors` or `off`.

access_log_exclude.description: Paths left out of the access log.

access_log_file.description: A file the access log's JSON lines go to in place of the terminal, relative to the project.

hosts.description: Names the development certificate covers besides localhost.

https_only.description: Serve HTTPS alone, HTTP redirecting to it.

reload_dirs.description: Directories watched, relative to the project; the project when empty.

reload_exclude.description: Patterns that never trigger a reload.

slow.description: How long a request may take before `errors` shows it.

timestamps.description: Whether every line on the terminal carries the full UTC time.

tls_cert.description: A certificate chain to serve, relative to the project.

tls_key.description: Its private key, relative to the project.

Scaling.description: The `scaling` table of a release, a worker group or a `[tool.muru]` table: the mode, the bounds, and the windows and budgets that keep the autoscaler from churning. The release's own table is the default group's.

churn_budget.description: Reaps allowed per hour per release before scale-in is suspended.

hold_after_growth.description: No scale-in this long after a scale-out.

host_idle_timeout.description: How long the release's host stays once every group has scaled to zero, after which it stops too and the next request starts it again; it stays while the release runs when omitted. In the release's own scaling table.

idle_reap_after.description: A group wholly idle this long scales in without waiting for the scale-in window.

max_spare.description: Spare mode: scale in while more idle workers than this remain.
max_spare.x-default: the larger of 3 and a quarter of `max_workers`

max_step_up.description: The most workers one scale-out adds.

max_workers.description: The most workers; required by the spare and target modes.

min_lifetime.description: No worker younger than this is reaped.
min_lifetime.x-default: the larger of 15m and 30 times the time to ready

min_spare.description: Spare mode: scale out when fewer idle workers than this remain.

queue_wait_p95.description: Target mode: scale out while the p95 queue wait is over this, for example 100ms; off when absent.

reap_interval.description: At most one worker reaped per this interval.

scale_in_window.description: How long every scale-in condition must hold.

scale_out_window.description: How long a scale-out condition must hold.

slot_utilization.description: Target mode: the share of slots to keep busy, between 0 and 1.

ScalingMode.description: How a worker group is scaled.

oneOf.description: A fixed worker count, the default.
Keep between min_spare and max_spare idle workers, Apache-style.
Track a slot utilization and a queue wait target.

SecretRef.description: Which secret: a store declared in the daemon's file, and a key in it.

SecretValue.description: A secret reference in an `[env]` table.

as.description: How the value is delivered: `env` as the variable, or `file` as a file only the release's user can read, whose path is in `NAME_FILE`.

ServeSettings.description: The `[tool.muru.serve]` table (`[serve]` in muru.toml), and the file `MURU_SERVE_CONFIG` names: how `muructl serve` runs the application in a container. A key is a flag of the command in snake case, taking the flag's value; a list key takes the values the flag would be repeated with.

access_log_exclude.description: Paths left out of the access log.

admin_listen.description: Where the probes and metrics are served, IP:PORT or `off`.

admin_status.description: Whether `/status` is served on the admin port.

concurrency.description: Requests an ASGI worker's event loop takes at once.

factory.description: Whether the entrypoint is a factory.

hooks.description: The module providing the lifecycle hooks.

listen.description: Where the application is served, IP:PORT.

log_format.description: The lines on standard output: `text` (the default), or `json` for a log collector.

max_connections_per_client.description: Connections one client may have open.

max_lifetime.description: How long a worker lives before it is replaced.

max_requests.description: Requests a worker serves before it is replaced.

min_ready.description: The workers ready in every worker group for `/readyz` to pass.

preload.description: Whether the application is imported before the workers are forked: `auto`, `true` or `false`.

processes.description: Worker processes, or `auto` for the container's CPU limit, else the CPU count.

python.description: The interpreter: a path, or a request in uv's syntax. When absent, `/app/.venv` if there is no `VIRTUAL_ENV` and no project `.venv`, else the interpreter `muructl run` would find.

run_dir.description: Where everything written at run time goes.

runtime_dir.description: Where the image holds the runtime library.

shutdown_budget.description: How long the whole stop may take, the delay included.

shutdown_delay.description: How long the listener keeps accepting after SIGTERM, readiness failing, with every connection closing after its response.

slow.description: How slow a request is to count as an error for `access_log = "errors"`.

spool_quota.description: The most request bodies spooled to disk at once.

sync_threads.description: Threads for synchronous code called from an ASGI application.

timeout.description: Timeouts as NAME=DURATION, as `--timeout` takes them.

timestamps.description: Whether every line carries the full UTC time.

trusted_proxy.description: The proxies whose forwarding headers are applied: addresses, CIDR ranges, or loopback, private and unix. A proxy named here also gets a proxy's share of connections and keep-alive timeout.
trusted_proxy.x-default: loopback peers, for their forwarding headers alone

StaticDir.description: A directory of an application's own files, an entry of the `[[tool.muru.static]]` or `[[app.NAME.release.ID.static]]` array: a path prefix the edge serves from a directory under the release's source, with the application taking what no file answers. Served by `muructl run` and the daemon alike, from the release the request was routed to.

cache.description: The cache headers files are sent with.

case.description: `strict` (the default), which matches names as they are on disk, or `insensitive`.

dir.description: The directory, relative to the source directory, or absolute.

fallback.description: The file served for paths with no file of their own, for a single-page application under the prefix.

index.description: The files tried, in order, when a directory is requested.

path.description: The path prefix, such as `/static/`; the longest wins, on segment boundaries, and `/` is not allowed, since every path would then be looked up as a file first.

redirect_slash.description: Whether a directory asked for without a trailing slash is redirected to the slash form.

Timeouts.description: The `[timeouts]` table of a release or a `[tool.muru]` table: the timeouts the host enforces on its workers. The edge's own timeouts are the daemon's `[limits]`.

gil_stall_timeout.description: How long a worker may go with no thread running Python, or with no report to its host, before it is replaced as for the hard timeout.

hard_drain_grace.description: How long a worker being replaced is given to finish its other requests before it is told to stop.

hard_timeout.description: How long a request may run in a worker before the worker is replaced, for example 60s; off when absent. Must exceed the soft timeout by at least 5s.

loop_stall_timeout.description: How long an ASGI worker's event loop may go without running before the worker is replaced as for the hard timeout.

shutdown_timeout.description: How long a worker told to stop is given before it is killed, counted from when its WebSockets are closed.

soft_timeout.description: How long a request may run in a worker before it is interrupted by raising `muru.RequestTimeout` in its thread, for example 30s; off when absent.

websocket_drain_grace.description: How long a worker told to stop keeps its open WebSockets before it closes them with 1001.

description: The `[tool.muru]` table: defaults an application ships with. Every field is optional; what a command line or a release definition sets takes precedence.

accel_redirect.description: Treat an `X-Accel-Redirect` response header as an internal redirect, for the default mount and any mount that does not say otherwise.

build.description: When and how the environment is built.

bytecode.description: Where compiled bytecode goes under the daemon.

cgi_local_redirect.description: Treat a 200 response with a `Location` starting with `/` and no body as an internal redirect, the CGI convention.

commands.description: Commands the application declares, by name: run with the release on request, with inputs.

concurrency.description: Requests an ASGI worker's event loop takes at once.

env.description: Environment variables for the workers: a value, or a secret reference resolved when the release starts.

error_override.description: Replace the application's own error responses with error pages.

error_pages.description: Custom error pages, by status or status:reason.

factory.description: Whether the entrypoint is a factory returning the application.

grpc_web_origins.description: The origins whose pages may call the gRPC methods through gRPC-Web, or `*`.

handoff.description: The interface the entrypoint's requests may be handed to.

hooks.description: The module providing the lifecycle hooks.

logging.description: How Python logging is set up in the workers.

max_lifetime.description: How long a worker lives before it is replaced.

max_requests.description: Requests a worker serves before it is replaced.

memory.description: The memory policy for the workers.

preload.description: Whether the application is imported once, in the host, before the workers are forked from it.

processes.x-default: `1`; under `muructl serve`, the container's CPU limit, else the CPU count

python.description: The interpreter: a path, or a request in uv's syntax such as "3.13", "3.14t" or ">=3.12".

reflection.description: Serve gRPC server reflection for the registered services.

run.description: How `muructl run` serves the project, which the daemon ignores.

scaling.description: How the default group is scaled; static when absent.

sendfile_header.description: A second response header honoured as `X-Muru-Sendfile` is, such as `X-Sendfile` for the frameworks that send that one.

sendfile_roots.description: Directories a path in an `X-Muru-Sendfile` response header must lie in for the edge to serve the file, for the default mount and any mount that does not say otherwise; with none every hint is refused.

serve.description: How `muructl serve` runs the project in a container, which the daemon and `muructl run` ignore.

static.description: The application's own static directories, served by the edge from the release's source, which is the project directory under `muructl run`.

sync_threads.description: Threads for synchronous code called from an ASGI application.

timeouts.description: The timeouts the host enforces on its workers.

title: The project's [tool.muru] table
